title: The Amplification Shift: From Walled Gardens to Premium Media
summary: Crowded social feeds mean up to 27% of younger audiences actively tune ads out. By transporting your top creator and social-first assets into CTV and trusted editorial environments, you can extend creative shelf-life, tap into higher consumer trust, and unlock incremental reach.
body_markdown:
High-performing creator content and social-first video represent some of the most compelling investments in modern marketing. Major social platforms and walled garden networks remain highly effective for discovery, rapid audience acquisition, and real-time community engagement. But when distribution stops at social, so does the opportunity for your strongest assets to work elsewhere.


***[The Connected Consumer Blueprint, Volume 2,](https://view-su2.highspot.com/viewer/32de4f026d4c685bdb05b51bc299f87f)*** explores how brands can extend social-first creative beyond walled gardens and into premium editorial and connected TV environments.


## **The social feed isn’t the only place your audience pays attention**


Social’s speed and scale are strengths. But crowded feeds also create a challenge: reaching people doesn’t necessarily mean they are receptive to another ad.


Our research with Censuswide highlights that friction:


- 23% of consumers describe social-feed ads as “overwhelming and repetitive.”
- 20% say they actively tune them out.
- 27% of 18–24-year-olds say they ignore social-feed advertising because of ad volume overload.


This isn’t about replacing social media; it’s about increasing the shelf-life and ROI of your creative investments. By transporting vertical, creator-led assets into premium open-web editorial streams and big-screen television environments, brands unlock massive incremental reach among high-value audiences who are actively leaning in.


## **The amplification shift has to do with trust**


Simply said, the environment around an ad matters. Our research shows that 44.1% of surveyed social media users report trusting ads on major news and lifestyle websites more than ads in social feeds. Among 25–34-year-olds, that figure rises to 55.1%.

By surrounding authentic creator content with the institutional authority of premium editorial publishing, brands transform fleeting social sparks into sustained commercial impact.
